raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Ready for review.

## Overview

With eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, a prefix that keeps hitting the GPU prefix cache is the first thing evicted from the CPU cache, because its CPU copy never leaves its first-store LRU position. When a request with a GPU prefix hit is admitted, this PR moves the CPU copy of that prefix to the MRU end.

## Claims

- Eager mode keeps hot GPU-hit prefixes on CPU; lazy mode is unchanged.
- Kimi-K3 agentic disaggregated benchmark on MI355X at `be4275d22`: +8.7% total tok/s/GPU, mean TTFT 8.6 s to 5.3 s.

## Validation

- New `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_lru` (full attention) and `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_mamba_boundary` (attention + Mamba) fail on main and pass here. The second also catches refreshing only full attention, freeing in forward order, or refreshing at lookup.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/` and the SimpleCPUOffload connector, metrics and NIXL unit tests at `be4275d22`: 179 passed, 8 skipped (optional integration tests). pre-commit clean.
- End to end: one run per configuration, below.

<details><summary>End-to-end benchmark</summary>

Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, `MultiConnector` of MoRIIO and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (`lazy_offload: false`, 1.8 TB) on the prefill instance. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97`; "after" mounts this PR's `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` at `be4275d22`, ported onto the nightly; server config otherwise identical. Both ran on 2026-10-26 with prefill on the same node; decode nodes differ.

| | [before](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40286897952/job/121452690051) | [after](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40300366703/job/121496601447) |
|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s/GPU | 9783 | 10638 (+8.7%) |
| TTFT mean / p90 | 8.58 s / 21.71 s | 5.27 s / 11.08 s |
| TPOT p90 | 20.50 ms | 20.08 ms |
| Prefill tokens recomputed per request | 6160 | 5178 (-15.9%) |
| Prompt tokens loaded from CPU | 5.0% | 5.4% |

The first revision (`edf0671ce`, refresh at lookup) measured [9658](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38850989926) to [10616](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39054120919) tok/s/GPU in the same setup.

</details>

## Details

Root cause on the prefill instance:

1. Turn 1 computes prefix X; the eager store copies X to CPU.
2. Later turns hit X on GPU. Eager stores skip blocks already on CPU, so X's CPU copy is never touched.
3. Other requests' stores evict CPU blocks in LRU order, so X goes first although it is the hottest prefix.
4. When GPU pressure later evicts X, the next turn misses both tiers and recomputes X.

In eager mode, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` records the GPU hit length and `update_state_after_alloc` refreshes that prefix once at admission, so a request waiting for blocks does not repeat the CPU lookup each step. The refresh runs `cpu_coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` over the prefix, then touches and frees the result in reverse order like `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.free`: every full-attention block, the sliding window and the Mamba state at the boundary.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body: I faced this issue and caused quite heavy drop in prefix cache hits under long context + high concurrency with kimi-k3 which was solved after patching this fix cc: @NickLucche

Thanks! Only took a very rough pass but this looks like a good direction, in the sense that this is a more correct behavior for inclusive cache. 

My high level concern is on the impl, which doesn't feel very clean to me. For example, I am thinking sth like upon SimpleCPUOffload lookup, if the position starts from the middle of a request, we touch those corresponding prefix blocks (like all full attn blocks and boundary of SWA/mamba states) in the CPU space. Or maybe I simplified the problem too much. Anyway happy to discuss

@ivanium Thanks for the advice. I made a new commit and now the impl is: When lookup starts after a GPU hit, eager mode runs `cpu_coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` over that prefix and touches and frees the result: every full-attention block, the sliding window and the Mamba state at the boundary. Should be cleaner now. Welcome for further suggestions.
@ivanium I have refactored according to your suggestion and re-tested the PR. Results are still good. Please take a look again. Thanks a lot~

@@ -31,6 +31,7 @@
 from vllm.v1.core.block_pool import BlockPool
 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheBlocks, KVCacheManager
 from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import (
+    KVCacheBlock,
     get_request_block_hasher,
     init_none_hash,
     make_block_hash_with_group_id,
@@ -1329,6 +1330,68 @@ def test_touched_blocks_survive_eviction() -> None:
         assert cached is not None, f"req_a block {i} should survive (was touched/MRU)"
 
 
+def test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_lru() -> None:
+    """Eager mode: a prefix that hits on GPU keeps its CPU copy at the MRU end."""
+    fix = make_scheduler(num_cpu_blocks=5, num_gpu_blocks=16, lazy=False)
+    sched = fix.scheduler
+
+    # Fill all 4 usable CPU blocks: req_a is LRU, req_b is MRU.
+    req_a = make_request(num_blocks=2)
+    req_b = make_request(num_blocks=2)
+    kv_a = _alloc_and_register(fix, req_a, 2)
+    kv_b = _alloc_and_register(fix, req_b, 2)
+    sched.update_state_after_alloc(req_a, kv_a, num_external_tokens=0)
+    sched.update_state_after_alloc(req_b, kv_b, num_external_tokens=0)
+    meta = sched.build_connector_meta(
+        make_scheduler_output(
+            {req_a.request_id: 2 * BLOCK_SIZE, req_b.request_id: 2 * BLOCK_SIZE},
+            new_reqs={
+                req_a.request_id: kv_a.get_block_ids(),
+                req_b.request_id: kv_b.get_block_ids(),
+            },
+        )
+    )
+    simulate_store_completion(sched, meta.store_event)
+
+    # req_a's prefix is reused and hits entirely on GPU.
+    req_a2 = Request(
+        request_id="req-a2",
+        prompt_token_ids=req_a.prompt_token_ids,
+        sampling_params=req_a.sampling_params,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        mm_features=None,
+        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(BLOCK_SIZE, sha256),
+    )
+    assert sched.get_num_new_matched_tokens(req_a2, 2 * BLOCK_SIZE) == (0, False)
+    sched.update_state_after_alloc(
+        req_a2, KVCacheBlocks(blocks=([],)), num_external_tokens=0
+    )
+
+    # Storing 2 new blocks evicts the 2 LRU blocks, which are now req_b's.
+    req_c = make_request(num_blocks=2)
+    kv_c = _alloc_and_register(fix, req_c, 2)
+    sched.update_state_after_alloc(req_c, kv_c, num_external_tokens=0)
+    meta2 = sched.build_connector_meta(
+        make_scheduler_output(
+            {req_c.request_id: 2 * BLOCK_SIZE},
+            new_reqs={req_c.request_id: kv_c.get_block_ids()},
+        )
+    )
+    simulate_store_completion(sched, meta2.store_event)
+
+    cache_map = sched.cpu_block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block
+
+    def cpu_cached(req: Request) -> list[bool]:
+        return [
+            cache_map.get_one_block(make_block_hash_with_group_id(h, 0)) is not None
+            for h in req.block_hashes[:2]
+        ]
+
+    assert cpu_cached(req_a) == [True, True]
+    assert cpu_cached(req_b) == [False, False]
+    assert cpu_cached(req_c) == [True, True]
+
+
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Test 5: Preemption no CPU block leak
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -2966,6 +3029,45 @@ def test_finished_eager_store_does_not_duplicate_completed_partial_tail() -> Non
     assert len(finish_meta.store_cpu_blocks) == len(stored)
 
 
+def test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_mamba_boundary() -> None:
+    """A hybrid GPU prefix hit refreshes the CPU attention blocks and the Mamba
+    state at the hit boundary, not older Mamba states, once admitted."""
+    block_size = 4 * BLOCK_SIZE
+    fix = _make_hybrid_attention_mamba_scheduler(block_size=block_size)
+    sched = fix.scheduler
+    cpu_pool = sched.cpu_block_pool
+    req = _make_cp_request(num_blocks=2, virtual_block_size=block_size)
+    other = _make_cp_request(num_blocks=2, virtual_block_size=block_size)
+
+    def cache_on_cpu(request: Request, group_id: int) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
+        blocks = cpu_pool.get_new_blocks(2)
+        cpu_pool.cache_full_blocks(
+            request=request,
+            blocks=blocks,
+            num_cached_blocks=0,
+            num_full_blocks=2,
+            block_size=sched.group_block_sizes[group_id],
+            kv_cache_group_id=group_id,
+        )
+        return blocks
+
+    attention, mamba = cache_on_cpu(req, 0), cache_on_cpu(req, 1)
+    newer = cache_on_cpu(other, 0)
+    cpu_pool.free_blocks([*attention, *mamba])
+    cpu_pool.free_blocks(newer)
+
+    lru_before = cpu_pool.free_block_queue.get_all_free_blocks()
+    assert sched.get_num_new_matched_tokens(req, 2 * block_size) == (0, False)
+    assert cpu_pool.free_block_queue.get_all_free_blocks() == lru_before
+    sched.update_state_after_alloc(
+        req, KVCacheBlocks(blocks=([], [])), num_external_tokens=0
+    )
+
+    lru_order = cpu_pool.free_block_queue.get_all_free_blocks()
+    assert lru_order[-3:] == [mamba[1], attention[1], attention[0]]
+    assert lru_order.index(mamba[0]) < lru_order.index(newer[0])
+
+
 def test_external_lookup_rejects_misaligned_local_prefix(caplog_vllm) -> None:
     scheduler_block_size = 4 * BLOCK_SIZE
     fix = _make_hybrid_attention_mamba_scheduler(block_size=scheduler_block_size)

@@ -449,6 +458,16 @@ def update_state_after_alloc(
                 num_stored_blocks=[0] * num_groups,
             )
 
+        if num_local_tokens := self._pending_local_hits.pop(req_id, None):
+            # Eager CPU is inclusive: a GPU prefix hit also uses the CPU copy,
+            # but eager stores skip it, so move it to the MRU end here.
+            prefix_hit, _, _ = self.cpu_coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit(
+                request.block_hashes, num_local_tokens

+            prefix_blocks = [b for grp in prefix_hit for b in grp if not b.is_null]
+            self.cpu_block_pool.touch(prefix_blocks)
+            self.cpu_block_pool.free_blocks(reversed(prefix_blocks))
+
         # Pop the CPU hit cached by get_num_new_matched_tokens(). The
         # found blocks were pinned there to survive LRU eviction in the window
         # between get_num_new_matched_tokens() and this matching call.
@@ -1232,6 +1251,7 @@ def request_finished(
         pending = self._pending_cpu_hits.pop(req_id, None)
         if pending is not None:
             self._free_pending_cpu_hit(pending)
+        self._pending_local_hits.pop(req_id, None)
 
         # Handle load: defer cleanup if load is in-flight
         load_state = self._reqs_to_load.get(req_id)

         for pending in self._pending_cpu_hits.values():
             self._free_pending_cpu_hit(pending)
         self._pending_cpu_hits.clear()
+        self._pending_local_hits.clear()
 
         self._abandoned_store_event_to_blocks.update(self._store_event_to_blocks)
